glosses: to be financially independent, to support oneself without assistance from others

examples.text: Een kalkoen blijft heerlijk mals als je deze tijdens het braden regelmatig bedruipt met braadvocht.

glosses: zich ~: zich redden, voor zichzelf zorgen

examples.text: Oh, die weet zich wel te bedruipen, hoor!

glosses: To sew with long or loose stitches, as for temporary use, or in preparation for gathering the fabric.

examples.text: He bastes the coat together with thick white thread almost like string, using stitches big enough to be ripped out easily later.

glosses: To sprinkle flour and salt and drip butter or fat on, as on meat in roasting.

examples.text: Ice Cold Daydream" bastes the bayou funk of the Meters in swirling psychedelia, while "Sweet Thang," a swampy blues cowritten with his dad, sounds like something from Dr. John's "Night Tripper" phase.

glosses: A basting; a sprinkling of drippings etc. in cooking.

examples.text: "Just like a leg of mutton being roasted before a slow fire without any one to give it a baste," groaned the old man.

glosses: To beat with a stick; to cudgel.

examples.text:
July 1660, Samuel Pepys, Diaries
One man was basted by the keeper for carrying some people over on his back through the waters.

glosses: Esparcir gotas menudas de agua o de otro líquido.

examples.text: -Tome vuestra merced, señor licenciado: rocíe este aposento, no esté aquí algún encantador de los muchos que tienen estos libros, y nos encanten, en pena de las que les queremos dar echándolos del mundo.

glosses: Lanzar objetos de modo que se dispersen.
Gratificar –en juegos de azar– un jugador a quien le facilita dinero.

examples.text: Mantener a los perros no deseados fuera de tu patio puede ser un reto si tu propiedad no está completamente cercada. Los perros son curiosos por naturaleza e irán a investigar olores interesantes como el olor de tus propios perros y el olor de otros que podrían haber pasado por allí. Rociar vinagre o jugo de limón para repeler a los perros es una opción que se puede utilizar sin incurrir en altos costos y sin causar daño a tus perros o a otros

glosses: Of an individual or business, to earn enough to cover one's expenses.

examples.text: The train service averaged four trains each way on weekdays, and a single Sunday train in each direction, but though the line continued to pay its way until the first world war, immediately afterwards receipts dropped to such an extent that on February 8, 1924, a meeting was called to consider closing the line.

Only a year ago it would have needed a "super-Micawber" to be optimistic that the railways would once again pay their way. But it was no longer a pipe dream that B.R. could make a profit, the way to do it was now clear.
